title: UrjaRakshak
description: Physics-based energy integrity and grid intelligence platform for detecting theft, losses, and anomalies across power distribution networks.
longDescription: UrjaRakshak is a physics-first energy integrity platform that protects power infrastructure using thermodynamic ground truths combined with machine learning. Every analysis begins with an I²R loss model and works outward — never the other way. The system computes a Grid Health Index (GHI) from five subscores (Physics Balance, Anomaly Severity, Compliance, Transformer Status, and Drift Integrity), flags suspicious meter readings via a 3-gate anomaly engine (physics + z-score + Isolation Forest), auto-generates inspection tickets when residuals exceed 8% or GHI drops below 50, and chains every action to a SHA-256 audit ledger. Optional AI interpretation via Claude or GPT-4o-mini produces structured narratives. Designed for infrastructure-scope analysis only — individual attribution is deliberately out of scope.
architectureDescription:
Frontend (Next.js 14) → FastAPI backend → PostgreSQL/Supabase

Data flow:
1. CSV upload → per-meter Z-score anomaly detection → MeterReading table
2. Physics validation → I²R losses + transformer losses → residual = actual − expected
3. GHI engine → PBS·0.35 + ASS·0.20 + CS·0.15 + TSS·0.15 + DIS·0.15 → score 0–100
4. Risk classifier → inspection ticket auto-created if residual > 8% or GHI < 50
5. AI interpretation (optional) → Claude / OpenAI generates structured narrative
6. Drift detection → PSI + K-S test → auto-retrain trigger if SEVERE
7. Audit → SHA-256 hash chain on every action (tamper-evident ledger)
